intro
Creative work doesn't end with its creator.
statement
Fans remix it. Sculptors rebuild it. Studios want to license it. But permission, and payment, never follow the work.
meet
This is Canon. On NEAR, every work is an NFT that owns its own wallet, with no keys anyone can steal or misuse.
explore
Here's Ember Field, and the family of derivatives built on it. Each one approved, on-chain, by the work it came from.
clearance
Open the motion loop. Canon checks the entire lineage. Every ancestor allows commercial use, so it's cleared.
payout
Now watch one licence pay everyone. A single payment splits up the family tree, to every vault and every contributor, in one transaction.
checkout
Before a studio pays, it sees exactly who gets what, to the last decimal.
collection
The studio receives a licence NFT. Hold it, and the source files unlock.
register
Creators submit new derivatives, and only the original's current owner can approve them into the canon.
blocked
And if any ancestor forbids commercial use, the licence simply can't be issued.
explorer
Every step is a real transaction on NEAR, that anyone can open.
security
Sell the NFT, and its income moves with it. The seller is locked out. Every attack we could think of was tried on-chain, and refused.
proof
Forty-one tests. Forty-one live transactions. Zero admin keys. Not even ours.
end
Canon. Creative IP that pays its whole family tree. Live now, on NEAR.
